About The Author

William Halford

William Halford is a storyteller shaped by discipline, service, and a lifelong curiosity about the unknown. Born in Forrest City, Arkansas, he built a career grounded in precision and responsibility, serving as an Air Traffic Controller in the United States Air Force before continuing his professional journey within the U.S. Army Civil Service. Alongside his technical achievements, William carried a deep passion for imagination and exploration, one that ultimately found its voice through writing.

POR! Prince of Borland reflects not only his creative vision but also his perseverance, faith, and the unwavering support of his family. With a background that blends structure and imagination, William brings a unique perspective to science fiction, one that is both grounded and expansive, driven by curiosity, purpose, and storytelling that reaches beyond worlds.

Six themes

About The Book

01

Parallel Worlds & Alternate Realities

A central concept is the existence of another world (Borland), emphasizing the idea that reality may extend far beyond what we understand. It introduces readers to advanced civilizations, different ecosystems, and alternate timelines.

02

Survival & Adaptation

The harsh and unfamiliar environment of Borland forces Billy to adapt physically, mentally, and emotionally. The book focuses on resilience, quick learning, and the human ability to survive in extreme conditions.

03

Loyalty, Friendship & Loss

Billy’s bond with Kim represents loyalty and the emotional cost of separation. The story captures the pain of leaving behind loved ones and the weight of unresolved connections.

04

Good vs Evil

The subplot involving Decragon introduces betrayal, jealousy, and internal conflict within power structures, reinforcing the timeless struggle between loyalty and ambition.

05

Moral Responsibility & Choice

Billy is constantly faced with choices that define his character: whether to return home, stay, fight, love, or lead. The narrative reinforces accountability and personal responsibility.

06

Time Displacement & Consequences

The difference in time flow between Earth and Borland adds depth to the narrative, showing how choices impact relationships, aging, and life paths in unexpected ways.

Testimonials

What My Reader Says

“A hidden gem in science fiction.”

I didn’t expect to get this immersed, but the story pulls you in from the very beginning. The transition from a normal college setting to an entirely new world is handled really well. The world-building is vivid, and Borland feels alive. Billy’s growth throughout the story is what kept me hooked. Definitely worth the read.

”

“Creative, adventurous, and emotionally grounded.”

What stood out to me was the balance between adventure and emotion. It’s not just about another world. It’s about belonging, purpose, and the choices we make. The relationship between Billy and Sharna adds a strong emotional layer. The ending especially stayed with me.

”

“A unique take on interdimensional travel.”

The concept of the metallic box and the portal is simple but effective. The Nahkvay creatures and Borland’s structure were particularly interesting. At times, I wanted even more detail about the world, but overall, it’s a very engaging read with a lot of imagination behind it.

”

“You can feel the author’s passion in every chapter.”

This book feels personal. It’s clear the author invested time and heart into building this story. The pacing keeps things moving, and there’s always something happening, whether it’s discovery, conflict, or character development. It’s the kind of book you don’t want to rush through.

”

“Strong storytelling with a classic sci-fi feel.”

It reminded me of older sci-fi adventures where exploration and character growth were the focus. Billy’s journey from student to warrior is satisfying to follow. The themes of loyalty and sacrifice are handled really well.

”
